topic: Sandbox-bwrap-Nix: Lightweight Sandbox for AI Agents and Experiments

key_points: Bubblewrap (bwrap) is a low-level unprivileged sandboxing tool used by Flatpak
Uses Linux user namespaces to allow unprivileged users to build sandboxes
Creates new mount namespace with tmpfs root, invisible from host
Supports PID, network, IPC, UTS namespaces and seccomp filters
Not a complete sandbox with a security policy — arguments define the security model
Uses PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS to prevent setuid binary escapes
~10ms overhead, no Docker or VMs needed
Cross-platform process sandboxing powered by OpenAI Codex's runtime
Deny-by-default: writes, network, env vars blocked unless explicitly allowed
Credential injection: API keys never visible inside sandbox, substituted at proxy level
File access control with allow/deny read/write paths
Network filtering by domain, clean environment inheritance
SDKs for Rust, TypeScript, Python with consistent API
~10ms overhead, ~7MB memory, single binary, no Docker/VMs
macOS (Seatbelt) and Linux (Bubblewrap + Seccomp + Namespaces) support
Wraps commands in sandbox blocking network by default, restricts filesystem
Works with Claude Code, Codex, Amp, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode
Built-in templates for common workflows (code, npm, etc.)
Violation monitoring mode (-m) for real-time logging of blocked requests
Cross-platform: macOS (sandbox-exec) + Linux (bubblewrap)
Config via fence.jsonc with extends/inheritance chain
Command blocking for dangerous commands like rm -rf, git push
NixOS microVM environments for AI coding agents using cloud-hypervisor
Full kernel-level isolation per project directory
Nix flake-driven configuration with pre-installed claude-code and opencode
Host /nix/store shared read-only across VMs — packages built once reused everywhere
~500ms boot on Linux (KVM), ~2-3s on macOS (QEMU)
Secrets injected via SSH into /run/nixcage-secrets tmpfs, never on disk
Heavier than bwrap but provides full VM isolation
Extremely lightweight, security-hardened, declarative container runtime for agents
Three modes: Agent (ephemeral), Strict Agent (fail-closed), Production (long-running)
12ms cold start vs Docker's ~500ms — near bare-metal performance
Uses cgroups, namespaces, pivot_root, capabilities, seccomp, Landlock LSM
Nix-native with first-class NixOS module support
gVisor integration for enhanced security, GPU passthrough support
Deny-by-default egress, per-service seccomp profiles with SHA-256 pinning

angles: Bubblewrap + Nix-shell provides the lightest-weight sandbox for AI agents — no Docker daemon, no VMs, just Linux kernel namespaces
The 2026 trend is moving away from Docker containers toward bwrap-based sandboxing for AI agent workloads due to startup latency and resource overhead
Credential injection (Zerobox pattern) solves the API key security problem — agent never sees the real key, only a placeholder
Nix + bwrap is a natural combination: Nix provides reproducible environments, bwrap provides isolation — together they give reproducible isolation
Most AI agent sandboxing solutions are DIY (HN consensus), creating a gap for a standardized how-to guide
Fence and Zerobox show the emerging pattern: deny-by-default with explicit allowlists for filesystem, network, and env vars
The spectrum from bwrap (lightest, ~10ms) → Docker (~500ms) → Firecracker/Nixcage (VM-level) → Nucleus (hardened container) lets users choose isolation vs speed tradeoffs
